paper: Profit Mirage: Revisiting Information Leakage in LLM-based Financial Agents

system_scope.SYS-FINLAKE-BENCH: out-of-scope leakage/memorization question-answer benchmark; FinLeak-Bench is the body/appendix alias

headline_strategy: FactFin converts real-time price, factor, and factorized-news state into executable buy/sell/hold code with a Strategy Code Generator and RAG, evolves candidate code with MCTS, and selects the strategy that balances factual performance against counterfactual prediction consistency, confidence invariance, and input-dependency scores.
headline_selection_basis: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 identify the optimized generated program C*—not the FinLake/FinLeak QA benchmark, a baseline agent, or buy-and-hold—as FactFin's proposed trading policy.
missing_headline_objects: the executable SCG language, function signature, package surface, sandbox and parser
all runtime prompts beyond one explicitly simplified template and all immutable model requests/responses
the RAG corpus, chunks, index, query construction, distances and retrieved records
the initial strategy code, MCTS node/action/branch definitions and every evolved strategy
the strategy evaluator, rollouts, reward, budget, convergence/stopping rule and random seeds
counterfactual generators, perturbation magnitudes, constraints, scenarios and alpha/beta/gamma objective weights
the original Yahoo/Alpaca price/news snapshots, exact factors, lookbacks and point-in-time rules
position quantities/weights, capital, inventory, shorting/leverage and signal-to-fill timing
numeric transaction costs, slippage, orders, fills, cash ledger and dated NAV
the train/validation split, repetitions, uncertainty, baseline snapshots and environment lock
material_validity_findings: FinLake-Bench in the abstract conflicts with FinLeak-Bench throughout the body and appendix.
The exact-equality benchmark equation conflicts with interval, partial, magnitude and qualitative scoring examples.
Fine-tuning data span January 2020-December 2022 while the stated test interval is January-June 2022, with no held-out-row definition.
FactFin/TSLA maximum-drawdown signs and rankings conflict across the result table and prose.
The claimed 1.4x Sharpe improvement is not supported by the displayed per-asset table means.
The pre/post-cutoff comparison changes calendar regimes and does not causally isolate memorization.

rejected_substitutes.route: Treat FinLake/FinLeak-Bench as the headline strategy
rejected_substitutes.reason: It is a leakage/memorization QA benchmark and produces no stock weights or returns.

rejected_substitutes.route: Run the simplified SCG prompt through a current GPT-4o endpoint
rejected_substitutes.reason: The prompt explicitly omits changing templates, examples, language/runtime contract, RAG observations, MCTS state and the evaluator; any resulting program would be a new strategy.

rejected_substitutes.route: Implement Algorithm 1 with chosen counterfactual weights
rejected_substitutes.reason: The perturbations, alpha/beta/gamma weights, search grammar, reward and convergence rule are missing, so the printed loop does not select one policy.
Buy-and-hold is a diagnostic comparator rather than FactFin, and the pinned current provider matches 0/6 displayed cells.

rejected_substitutes.route: Infer trades from reported FactFin tables or curves
rejected_substitutes.reason: Aggregate metrics and raster paths do not identify dates, actions, quantities, costs or the generated program.

result_policy: No leakage-benchmark score, simplified-prompt output, completed pseudocode, current-provider baseline, or backcast paper result is entered as a FactFin monthly return. The positive FactFin claims remain unresolved, not falsified.
